_about: Versioned certification record for every advertised Runtime Provider Interface route (#596). Provider cells are capabilities.json's supported_profiles x supported_harnesses per provider; harness cells are base.py's launch table x {ro, rw}. Each route group names its tier, evidence paths, explicit limitations and, for a refusal, the typed refusal. An upstream version or commit that was never recorded stays null (rendered `unknown`) and is never guessed. A provider bound to a pin (`upstream.pin`) goes STALE — every one of its cells reads `stale`, never its recorded tier — as soon as the pin's commit, version or live_receipts.version differs from `certified_against`; recheck the cells, bump record_version, re-record. runtime/scripts/certification.py validates and renders this file; docs/certification.md explains it and carries the first-run guide.

tiers.live-witnessed: A real upstream build and a real harness ran this route end to end; the evidence is a docs/runs/ report whose RUN: header binds (verifier=GREEN, cited as a mission's proof_evidence) and whose own inventoried artifacts name this exact route, quoted in witnessed.route. Exact upstream and harness versions are recorded.
tiers.fixture-tested: The fleet's own code for this route runs in CI against an in-repo fixture — a scripted upstream transport or the first_run.py inert worker. Proves the fleet's side of the route; proves nothing about the upstream build or the harness.
tiers.source-only: The route's launch or flags were written from reading upstream source or docs; no test drives this exact route.
tiers.unsupported: The fleet refuses this route before any launch, with the typed refusal named in `refusal`.
tiers.unavailable: Advertised, but no evidence of any kind exists in this repository: the route's state is unknown.

worker-start launches these with the host's agentDefaultArgs; the wrapper checks only that launch.effective carries the flag in its profile_flag map, which was read from Orca's source. No test drives these harnesses on the Orca route.

The provider is this repository's code, so each CI run certifies the commit it runs at; the first_run.py fixture drives create, dispatch, delivery, result, independent verify and retain/release through the public wrappers for every cell here.
The worker is an inert stand-in answering to each harness name: no real harness binary runs, and the launch flags themselves are source-read (see the harness cells).
CI runs the setsid backend only; tmux is exercised by tests/test_posix_provider.py on hosts that have it, and cmux by no test.

A ro worker has no tool to send mail. Where an exit monitor runs, its assignment names the line OPEN_FLEET_WORKER_DONE <dispatch-id> <succeeded|failed>, and when that line ends the harness's final answer (runtime/providers/transcript.py, the first-run report's reader) the monitor relays it as the worker's worker_done; the stand-in prints it in each harness's own output shape. A clean exit without the line is still worker_died (exit=0). Either way the coordinator takes the report from the transcript.
